name: Skin Lesion Detection in MATLAB
summary: A MATLAB graphical interface that processes a skin-lesion photograph through grey conversion, enhancement, binarisation and segmentation, then reports a classification with Energy and Contrast values.
result: One example run completed in 39.0 s, reporting Energy 0.411 and Contrast 0.188.
keywords: skin cancer melanoma lesion detection image processing segmentation texture energy contrast CNN dermatology

blocks.text: This MATLAB interface walks a skin-lesion photograph through a visible image-processing pipeline and returns a classification label. The pipeline stages are shown side by side so the user can see what each step does.

blocks.caption: Technology and methods
rows: MATLAB graphical interface with Train Database and Detect Melanoma functions.
Input image, grey conversion, enhancement, binarisation, segmentation, then classification, with each stage shown side by side.
Energy and Contrast readouts, a boundary plot in the classification panel, and elapsed processing time.
The project description also covers CNN architectures trained on large image databases for skin-cancer and tumour detection.

blocks.text: The menu offers Train Database, Detect Melanoma, About, Reset All and Exit. In the captured run the status line reads that detection completed, the classification reads "Highly Affected Melanoma", Energy is 0.411373, Contrast is 0.18796 and the total elapsed time is 39.0037 seconds.
This interface sits alongside broader work on CNN-based skin-cancer and tumour detection trained on large image databases, together with NLP, predictive modelling and anomaly detection.
Next steps: evaluate the pipeline on a public lesion dataset and compare its Energy and Contrast features with a CNN classifier.
